questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I heard from other students experiences that it was a very social school with a great location travel wise. It had a well-known lawschool and some great courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I struggled to find information about Covid-19. We had to go to Stockholm prior to our visit in order to receive a study permit. However, this is not a general concern.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a great international network to help you with everything you need, including finding accomodation and selecting courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult!! We were told that Covid made it harder than usually, so don't fear this. Search for UWO/Western housing facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: London is primarily a house-city with students living together 3-6 people in a house. I think it creates a more cozy atmosphere than in the bigger cities, seeing as it is easier to get a lot of people together

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only say 3 as we struggled to find a place. The place we ended up was great!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Each student has an amount of points that can be used to bit on preferred corses like an auction.
It looks confusing at first, but you have three chances to get i right and you are not under time pressure, so it is fine!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student community and office provided us with guidelines and were quick to answer additional questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. You can apply for more courses than you are required to, attend to all of them and then drop the ones you liked the least after a week or so. Also, you can apply for a Supplemental Writing Credit where you add 10 pages (double spaced) to one of your papers and get an extra credit that way. It helped me to not have to take an extra course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Suitable. Some were easier, some were harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Participation is a part of your grade in almost every course (from 10-25 % or so). You can either participate to get the best great possible or just take it chill and then deliver at your final paper/exam. I found that most exchange students did the later, and it worked out just fine for everyone.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Contract Issues
Statutory Interpretation
Anti-Corruption Law and Policy
Public International Law (+ Supplemental Writing Credit in this course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of my courses although I found Advanced Contract Issues a bit hard to follow, and the final assignment was difficult to write. It worked out fine though!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Study permit seeing as we travelled during covid. The permit alone was around 1200 DKK, but we had to fly to Stockholm to get it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less expensive to go to restaurants, bars, takeaway, etc. 
More expensive than expected to do groceries (although I think it was pretty similar to Denmark)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid a lot of the acivities were closed down. It was not a problem for me though

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A big recreational center with squash, basket, swimming pool and fitness center. Many clubs; karate, football, tennis etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any clubs due to covid. The city is full of tennis courts that you can play for free if you bring your own raquets.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Niagara Falls, Toronto, Tobermory and Lion's head are nearby. Also visit Montreal and British Columbia as well if your economy allows it. London has an Icehockey team as well, not that expensive to watch

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very outgoing and easy to be around

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How welcoming and helpful they were

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find housing through Facebook groups, don't live on campus
Go to Dollarbeer at Jacks on Mondays
Choose courses that ends with final assignments

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Western law has a perfect way of incorporating the exchange students into the eceryday life of the local students. Enjoy it!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A lot of new friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To relax - there is so many things you can attend and explore in Ontario (and the rest of Canada). Times goes by to fast

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
